Creador: CYPHER • Duración: 0:54

As sonic artists, we often don’t have any meaningful input on the subject matter or structure of the commercial projects we design for. We wanted to find a way to create an edit that would showcase our approach to crafting music and sound design to picture, not a ‘reel’, not a ‘manifesto’, but a series of sonic studies.

This first study came out of Joseph's interest in connecting his work in sound with sewing and textiles. The starting point was a jacket he had made, which gave us direct access to the fabrics, tools and machines involved in its construction, both as visual subjects and as sources for recording.

In our usual work, there's often a disconnect between what we see and what we hear. Sound design involves taking liberties with that relationship, using sounds that may have little to do with what's actually on screen but suggest the right movement, texture or feeling. Here, we could work with sounds that actually belonged to the subject, then manipulate and warp them without losing that underlying connection.

With limited visual resources, we relied on simple animation, scanned materials, basic image processing and textural footage. Rather than trying to disguise those limitations, we leaned into them, allowing the imagery to remain quite raw and minimal, giving the sound room to shape the rhythm and character of the edit.

As we worked through the project we found a nice relationship between sewing and sound. Each involves gathering, manipulating and assembling materials. This study gave us an opportunity to bring those practices together and experiment outside the usual constraints of a brief.

All of the designers at Cypher are makers at heart, we have spent years, decades, on the relationship between sound and motion. All of us have backgrounds in film and visual media, composition and recording arts.

This project began as one of Ordinary Folk’s earliest passion pieces in 2020. It went through multiple visual explorations and experiments, guided by a long list of talented collaborators. entry.summary: Araldica is illo's internal R&D project: a sound-reactive motion system built around heraldry, designed to scale across formats and stay in tune with the music, or even create it. In January 2026, the studio took heraldry as a personal brief, and one video came out of it: sharp, rhythmic, screened a
entry.content:
▶ Ver y reproducir video en FrameRate (1:00)

Creador: illo • Duración: 1:00

Araldica is illo's internal R&D project: a sound-reactive motion system built around heraldry, designed to scale across formats and stay in tune with the music, or even create it.

In January 2026, the studio took heraldry as a personal brief, and one video came out of it: sharp, rhythmic, screened at OFFF Barcelona, entirely built in Cavalry. Around the same time, we were deep into a project for a major international music player (whose name, contractually, we're not allowed to even think too loudly), and working so closely with sound changed how we read that video: it moved like music.

So we built a motion toolkit around it, a single visual system born from heraldic colour and pattern, from deep greens and sharp yellows to checkered geometries, reshaped to move in time with sound. From a playlist cover to a single track's artwork, from an in-app visual player to full video mapping on a wall, everything scales from the same source, the palette and pattern language staying recognisably heraldic at every size and format.

Inside the toolkit, two generative tools push it further. One turns sound into image: a track goes in, and its rhythm, genre and length shape a live animated visual, with a dedicated podcast mode where a coiling, serpent-like line shifts colour with every change of speaker. The other reverses it entirely: working in TouchDesigner, we scan the original Araldica footage colour by colour, translating it into music through Ableton.

entry.content:

Creador: Make Mami Proud • Duración: 1:52

Everybody lives with demons. Most people keep them quiet.

He gave his a face. Then a colour, a jacket, a way of walking — and once you draw something, it knows where you live. It points. It shouts. It waits at the end of the bed.
He fights them for a while. Everyone does.

Then he gets tired enough to stop, and the question changes. Not how to beat them. Whether they can be tamed. Whether they ever wanted anything from him but company.
Every frame drawn over by hand, until you can't tell which world is holding which.

Somewhere in there, a man burns out with a smile on his face and finds what he was looking for by losing track of it entirely.

NO AI. EVERY FRAME BY HAND.

Following Starling's 2025 rebrand, Buff partnered with the bank to create a suite of 16 social-first feature films promoting everyday banking tools. Alongside the campaign, we developed a motion framework that defined how the refreshed brand should behave in motion, creating a consistent animation language for future communications.

Working closely with Starling's team, we translated the brand's core attributes into a set of motion principles built around purposeful movement, confident pacing and clear, customer-focused storytelling. Every film balanced clarity, personality and trust, helping product features feel engaging without becoming tutorials or product demos.

Designed primarily for social, each short film follows a simple narrative structure to make budgeting, saving, payments and other everyday banking features easier to discover and understand. The result is a cohesive collection of films that showcase both Starling's product offering and its distinctive new identity in motion.

Finding love in unexpected places. Hétérocères reveals a nocturnal world where audiences are pulled into a ritualistic ceremony you were never meant to witness. Built in crafted 3D, the film establishes its horror aesthetic with hand-held cameras before transitioning into cinematic, expertly composed shots. The monochromatic opening quickly gives way to vibrant golds and lush flora as we’re given a glimpse into a world – built entirely in Blender – that suggests something much deeper and more complex.

What begins as something eerie reveals itself as a love story. Coup de Foudre’s command of contrast, character design, lighting and storytelling earns sympathy for creatures that, on first sight, you might expect to fear.

We crafted this neon-powered 2D spot to celebrate the evolution of Spotify's Mixing Tools, made in collaboration with Spotify's in-house Creative team.

A spaceship takes us on a playful journey through three distinct worlds inspired by the music: an abstract club scene, an ethereal lotus flower landscape, and a surreal city of giant faces.

The film seamlessly flows through tracks from Disclosure x Anderson .Paak, Jhené Aiko, and BLACKPINK visualizing an epic musical journey made possible by Mixing Tools.
